To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the majority of patients in our cohort were prescribed antimicrobials at least once during the study, that the majority of these prescriptions were inappropriate, and that the inappropriate prescriptions were most often due to lack of an infection or due to use of a broader spectrum agent than was necessary for the infection.
30% or more of the antimicrobial doses given to hemodialysis patients are inappropriate and that this inappropriate use is associated with a significant increase in the risk of hospitalization.
the majority of antimicrobial use among hemodialysis outpatients is appropriate and that there is a need to improve antimicrobial use in hemodialysis out-patients.
